title: #thewhostommy #goodmantheatre @Goodman Theatre
transcript: After having several friends tell me I’d be silly for missing it I got my stuff together and saw Goodman Theater's hotly-anticipated reimagining of The Who's Tommy. The show has been extended twice for good reason: it's a marvel. the set by David Korins and projections by Peter Nigrini provide a sensory overload now I'm generally not a fan of projections in theater but here they feel fully integrated into Pete Townshend’s iconic and heart-pumping score Des McAnuff returns to this material as director and it's a seamless experience the time flies by and in the title role Ali Louis Bourzgui (I hope I'm pronounced correctly) is captivating. Now the content of the show is something I'm still working through the story centers on trauma — both societally in the show's post-war era setting and when the show was written in ‘69 during the Vietnam War and in Tommy’s experience. Now I saw the original production back in ‘95 in Toronto as a teenager and it hits very differently as an adult. But I'll say they made some smart choices to stay true to the story yet not lean into the comedy of it all — say in Uncle Earnie. Now if you're a fan of The Who's Tommy you will love this production I really don't think you'll see a better production on it finally I was delighted to get an impromptu tour after the show by Hayley who is a veteran stagehand at the Goodman. the Goodman has invested a great deal into the backstage workings to make the show a visual feast in it it's just amazing I mean Acid Queen Low Fog? That is now my drag name. I gotta stand the stage of the Goodman! How cool is that? Go see this production! It plays throguh August *6th.*
classificationReason: Creator attended and reviewed a production at Goodman Theatre, but this is not the Broadway/West End production from the list (which is the-whos-tommy-2024)
